compliance.notes: A clean Arlingclose-model suite approved by full Council on 25 February 2026: prudential indicators, liability benchmark, borrowing strategy, counterparty/creditworthiness framework and the MRP policy statement are the strongest areas. The weakest areas are commercial proportionality (income dependence of ~17-18% of the net revenue stream is disclosed but never assessed against financial capacity, with no limits on service/commercial investment and no paras 51-53 compliance statement), an unspecified in-year reporting cycle (no mid-year, outturn or quarterly-monitoring commitments), and governance formalities (no four-clause adoption statement, no TM policy statement, no segregation-of-duties or member-training detail). The liability benchmark is a short-horizon table rather than a long-run chart, and specified/non-specified investment categories are not used.

news_drafts.headline: Internal Audit Consortium raises member councils' charges after £23,246 deficit
news_drafts.lead: The Internal Audit Consortium, which audits Chesterfield and three other councils, will increase what it charges them for its services in 2026/27 after recording a £23,246 deficit this year. The deficit arose from six months of agency staffing cover needed due to recruitment difficulties, a cost the consortium anticipated by retaining its prior-year surplus rather than returning it to members. Despite the deficit, internal audit delivered an unqualified opinion on all three councils' governance and control environments for 2025/26. The cost increase pushes Chesterfield's annual charge from £200,550 to £209,500. The consortium's working balance fell from £48,948 to £25,702, leaving considerably less buffer for future cost pressures, though it remains currently fully staffed.

news_drafts.headline: Chesterfield Council's merger plans paused, leaving structural budget gaps of £2.606m in 2027/28 rising to £4.662m by 2029/30
news_drafts.lead: Chesterfield Council's financial strategy has been upended by the government's decision to pause Local Government Reorganisation, invalidating plans built on a planned merger into a unitary authority on 1 April 2028. The council now faces a structural budget gap of £2.606m in 2027/28, rising to £4.662m by 2029/30, with no clear route to close it. The council's proposals to address the shortfall—efficiency savings of up to £1m and managed underspends of £0.3m to £0.5m—remain "planning assumptions rather than approved savings", according to its refreshed medium-term financial plan. The council has acknowledged it "may need to refocus on identifying and delivering its own transformation activity" rather than relying on the merger. With only three months until the December budget deadline, material savings work remains incomplete.

findings.headline: Member councils' charges increase in 2026/27, with Chesterfield paying £8,950 more annually.
findings.detail: To return to break-even, the consortium increased all member charges. Chesterfield's annual charge rose from £200,550 to £209,500. Other members' charges also increased: Bolsover £7,730 (to £180,880), NEDDC £7,780 (to £182,020), DDDC £2,890 (to £14,890). Total charges across members increased from £559,940 to £587,290.
findings.matters: Represents an unplanned cost increase in 2026/27 for member councils as they absorb the consortium's cost pressures.

findings.headline: Consortium working balance reduced by nearly half, from £48,948 to £25,702.
findings.detail: The 2025/26 deficit forced a substantial draw on reserves. The opening balance of £48,948 was reduced to £25,702 by year-end — a reduction of £23,246 (47%). For 2026/27, the opening balance is planned at £25,521, leaving significantly less buffer for future cost pressures.
findings.matters: Severely depleted reserves reduce the consortium's financial resilience and flexibility to handle future shocks.

findings.headline: Internal Audit Consortium had an unplanned deficit of £23,246 in 2025/26.
findings.detail: The consortium was budgeted to break-even originally in 2025/26, but a deficit of £23,427 emerged in the revised budget, with actual outturn at £23,246. This was driven by higher employee and support service costs than anticipated.
findings.matters: Reveals unexpected cost pressures in a council service and demonstrates the need to draw down reserves to cover unplanned deficits.

findings.headline: Recruitment difficulties led to six months of agency cover and subsequent staff turnover in the audit function
findings.detail: The Consortium experienced difficulties recruiting a BDC Senior Auditor, requiring six months of agency cover. Two part-time auditor posts were filled in 2025/26, but one BDC recruit left after five months and was replaced in August 2026. The Consortium is currently fully staffed, but the risk register identifies that departure of the Head of Internal Audit or a Senior Auditor would create future recruitment challenges.
findings.matters: Audit function continuity is essential for the control environment; the risk register signals that key-person dependencies could cause disruption if senior staff depart
findings.figures: 6 months of agency cover required; 1 of 2 part-time hires left after 5 months
findings.quote: recruitment remains a concern if the Head of Internal Audit or one of the Senior Auditors were to leave

findings.headline: The Audit Consortium recorded a £23,246 in-year deficit due to six months of agency staffing costs
findings.detail: The deficit arose from recruitment difficulties requiring temporary agency auditor cover for six months. The Council anticipated this cost and retained the prior-year surplus of £18,948, adding it to contingency rather than returning it to members. The result is a carry-forward balance to 2026/27 of £25,702, demonstrating the deficit was managed through reserve drawdown.
findings.matters: Finance directors monitor service deficits; this shows the Council anticipated and managed an unexpected staffing cost through retained reserves
findings.figures: £23,246 deficit; £18,948 prior-year surplus retained; £25,702 carry-forward balance to 2026/27
findings.quote: The financial year 2025/26 resulted in an in year deficit of £23,246. The deficit was due to the need to utilise an agency Auditor for 6 months due to recruitment difficulties.
